verdict.rationale: Gmail's own docs say offline mode lets you read, search, and reply without a connection. Messages sent offline are queued in an Outbox and sent automatically on reconnect. Only outgoing mail is shown to sync on reconnect, so the story's broader 'changes syncing' element is partly covered. missing for 10: documented sync of other offline changes (labels, archive/delete, read status, drafts) on reconnect, explicit composition of new messages offline beyond replies/sends, independent or hands-on corroboration of offline reliability

support.subject: As a power-user, I can read, search, and write email offline, with changes syncing when I reconnect

citations.quote: You can use Gmail offline to read, search, and reply to messages without an internet connection.
If you send a message offline, it's saved in a new "Outbox" folder. If you connect to the internet, the message is sent automatically.
